finding: The zoning approach considers land use, population and building density, environmental sensitivity and proposed regulations.
implication: Supports using several types of planning evidence. Does not define GIS-MCDA weights.

finding: The plan identifies seven main development-zone groups and subzones, including conservation zones.
implication: Use zoning in a separate spatial screening or comparison step, not as an input to independent core criteria.

finding: The plan states that general UDA planning and building regulations published under Gazette 2235/54 also apply.
implication: The raw suitability score cannot be described as development permission.

finding: Earth cutting on sloping land calls for relevant agency recommendations and a stated boundary protection measure.
implication: Slope has planning relevance, but this is NOT a universal slope-in-degrees suitability cutoff.

finding: Access-road width and UDA decision-making affect some proposals for development.
implication: OSM road proximity and density are access indicators, not proof of actual parcel access.

finding: Korathota highland conservation zone rules distinguish land up to 25 m above sea level.
implication: 25 m is zone-specific; do NOT apply a 25 m elevation threshold to all Kaduwela grids.

finding: Dedigamuwa highland conservation rules distinguish land at or below versus above 30 m elevation. Also see printed page 215.
implication: 30 m is zone-specific; do NOT apply a 30 m elevation threshold to all Kaduwela grids.

finding: Highly sensitive conservation areas include formally protected wetlands with restricted permitted uses.
implication: Use protected-area status as a later constraint. Not all permissible activities are ordinary construction.

finding: Low-sensitivity conservation zones also have defined permitted uses and conditions.
implication: Do not label every conservation zone as identical or automatically prohibit every use.

finding: Wetland-zone rules address uncertain boundaries, site surveys, drainage and flood-retention functions.
implication: Separate future wetland screening needs mapped boundaries and may require site-specific review. Do not use a universal 20 m buffer.

finding: Named roads have listed building lines of 24 m, 15 m, 12 m or 9 m measured from the road centreline.
implication: These are named-road-specific requirements, not generic suitability-distance thresholds for every OSM road.
